title: Termwise direct sums of complexes of modules are direct sums in D(A)
statement: Let $A$ be a ring, let $D(A)$ be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of $A$-modules, and let $(K_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed family of cochain complexes of $A$-modules. Then the termwise direct sum $\bigoplus_{i\in I}K_i^\bullet$, together with the images in $D(A)$ of the coprojections $K_i^\bullet\to\bigoplus_{i\in I}K_i^\bullet$, is a direct sum (coproduct) of the $K_i^\bullet$ in $D(A)$.

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 07D9 (lemma-derived-products), clauses (1)-(2), applied to the Grothendieck abelian category of A-modules

proof.text: The coproduct of cochain complexes is computed degreewise by Mathlib HomologicalComplexLimits. Given chain maps f,g from this coproduct and homotopies between their restrictions to each summand, descend each component of the homotopies through the degreewise coproduct. The vanishing and homotopy equations hold after precomposition with each coprojection, so degreewise colimit extensionality proves them. This is the fully proved private helper coproduct_homotopy.

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 07D9 (lemma-derived-products), clauses (1)-(2), applied to the Grothendieck abelian category of A-modules

proof.text: The category ModuleCat.{max u v} R is Grothendieck abelian: transport the Mathlib instance for modules over ULift.{v} R through restriction of scalars along the ring equivalence ULift R ≃ R. Apply the existing Grothendieck K-injective resolution theorem to a complex representing an arbitrary object X of the derived category, obtaining an isomorphism e : X ≅ Q L with L K-injective.

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 07D9 (lemma-derived-products), clauses (1)-(2), applied to the Grothendieck abelian category of A-modules

proof.text: For K-injective L, Qh_map_bijective and fullness of the homotopy quotient imply that each morphism Q K → Q L has a chain-map representative, and that two chain maps with equal Q-images are homotopic. Transport through quotientCompQhIso using its naturality. These assertions are the fully proved private helpers derived_map_surjective and derived_map_homotopy.

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 07D9 (lemma-derived-products), clauses (1)-(2), applied to the Grothendieck abelian category of A-modules

proof.text: Given arrows a_i : Q K_i → X, lift a_i followed by e.hom to chain maps f_i : K_i → L and descend them to Sigma.desc f. Compose its Q-image with e.inv to obtain d; the coprojection equations follow from Sigma.ι_desc. For uniqueness, lift m followed by e.hom to g : ∐ K → L. The coprojection equations imply that each restriction of g is homotopic to the corresponding restriction of Sigma.desc f. Assemble these homotopies with coproduct_homotopy and use Q_map_eq_of_homotopy. Cancellation of e.hom proves uniqueness. Cofan.IsColimit.mk packages this existence and uniqueness into the required colimit.
